message.content:
Here are some of the major airports in the United States, known for their high passenger traffic, extensive flight networks, and significant economic impact:

| Airport | City | State | IATA Code | Notable Features |
|---------|------|-------|-----------|------------------|
| Hartsfield‑Jackson Atlanta International Airport | Atlanta | Georgia | ATL | Largest airport in the world by passenger traffic; major hub for Delta Air Lines. |
| Los Angeles International Airport | Los Angeles | California | LAX | Major gateway to Asia and Latin America; busiest international airport in the U.S. |
| Chicago O’Hare International Airport | Chicago | Illinois | ORD | One of the oldest major hubs; largest cargo hub in the world. |
| Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport | Dallas/Fort Worth | Texas | DFW | Largest airport by land area; major hub for American Airlines. |
| Denver International Airport | Denver | Colorado | DEN | Largest airport by land area in the U.S.; major hub for United Airlines. |
| John F. Kennedy International Airport | New York City | New York | JFK | Major gateway to Europe; one of the busiest airports in the U.S. |
| San Francisco International Airport | San Francisco | California | SFO | Major hub for flights to Asia; known for its sustainability initiatives. |
| Seattle–Tacoma International Airport | Seattle | Washington | SEA | Major hub for Alaska Airlines; key gateway to the Pacific Northwest. |
| Miami International Airport | Miami | Florida | MIA | Major hub for flights to Latin America and the Caribbean. |
| Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport | Phoenix | Arizona | PHX | Major hub for Southwest Airlines; one of the fastest-growing airports in the U.S. |

These airports serve as critical transportation hubs, connecting domestic and international destinations and supporting millions of passengers each year.
